title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare and say your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information. They may ask for your Medicare number or banking details.
example_message: "This is Medicare. We need to verify your information or your coverage will be canceled immediately. Please provide your Medicare number now."
red_flags: Caller threatens to cancel your benefits
Asks for your Medicare or Social Security number
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Package Delivery Texts
how_it_works: You get a text saying there is a problem with a package delivery and you need to click a link to fix it. The link may steal your information or install a virus.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please confirm your address by clicking here: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link to click or enter personal info
what_to_do: Do not click the link; delete the message and check with the delivery company using their official website.

title: Social Security Email Phishing
how_it_works: Scammers send emails pretending to be from the Social Security Administration, claiming there is a problem with your account. They ask you to click a link or call a number to fix it.
example_message: "We have detected suspicious activity on your Social Security account. Please click here to verify your information or call us at [fake number]."
what_to_do: Do not reply or click any links; go to the official Social Security website or call their real number.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook
how_it_works: Someone you meet on Facebook or another social media site quickly wants to start a relationship. Soon, they ask for money for an emergency or travel.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help with a sudden medical bill. Can you send me $500?"
red_flags: Asks for money or gift cards
Won't meet in person or video chat
what_to_do: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: A scammer calls pretending to be your grandchild or someone calling for them. They say there’s an emergency and need money right away, often asking you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in trouble and need money for bail. Please don’t tell mom and dad. Can you send $1,000 right away?"
red_flags: Caller claims to be a grandchild in trouble
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member directly to check the story.
